title: Cross-Leads Standup Digest — Oct 6 2026
content:
Meeting: Cross-team engineering leadership weekly
Date: 2026-10-06 09:30–10:30 PT
Location: Zoom / #eng-leads channel
Facilitator: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Marco H., Sana I., Kenji Y., Priya R., Liam O'C., Mei Chen (observability), Rajiv S. (serving-runtime), Tom B. (private-deployments) — partial list; see Slack thread for full.

Purpose: quick, actionable alignment across platform teams. Keep items time-boxed; surface blockers that need cross-org intervention. This doc is a lightweight digest — use for handoffs and follow-ups.

Topline updates (2-3 bullets per team — quick status + one ask):
- Serving Runtime (Rajiv): Canary rollout of v0.9.4 began yesterday — initial P99 memory spike on 512-length sequences. Root-cause suspected: LRU cache interaction with new sharding code path. Temporary mitigations: throttle new requests to canary pool and enable old cache behavior as fallback. Ask: platform-engineering to unblock canary by providing a transient higher-memory canary node (t-shirt: +n1-highmem) for 48–72h so we can get broader sample.
- Platform Scheduling (Aisha/Marco): Autoscaler policy update PR merged (autoscale: backoff-smarter). Two follow-ups: (1) need load-curve snapshots from production for last 14 days (SRE to provide), (2) coordinate with Dedicated to validate reserved pool sizing for low-latency customers. Ask: SRE/Sizing team to produce CSV by EOD Friday.
- Private Deployments (Tom): On-prem install 3.2 release blocked by KMS integration failing during bootstrap in gov region (keys not accessible due to network proxy rules). Workaround via manual key injection documented; long-term: need network rule exception. Ask: Security team to review proxy baseline and approve exception for installer traffic.
- Observability (Mei): New dashboard for token-level cost attribution is live in staging. Two missing pieces: (a) tagging at request origin (customer-route) sometimes null — instrumentation bug ticket INF-3347, (b) trace sampling rate needs bump for dedicated pool events. Ask: Dev teams to add route tags on library calls (PR guidance in Confluence page).
- Console & Rollouts (Priya): Rollout UI for A/B model routing is feature-frozen. Minor UX polish left; feature flag toggle will be ready for platform QA on Oct 8. Ask: QE to allocate 2 testers for Oct 8–9 cycle.
- Optimize (Sana): Cost-savings pilot with quantization heuristics finished pilot phase — demonstrated 18–24% token cost reduction for 8-bit profile on medium-length workloads. Caveat: slight BLEU/QA regressions in edge prompts; tracking with eval suite. Ask: Product to approve extended pilot for 4 additional customers.

Blockers and decisions (quick table-style notes):
- Memory spike in canary (serving-runtime) — decision: revert cache behavior for canary only until fix; target rollback window 2–4 hours tonight. Owner: Rajiv.
- Dedicated pool sizing for new customers — decision deferred: need numbers from SRE and sales commit sizes. Owner: Marco to coordinate.
- KMS proxy exceptions for on-prem installer — blocker for 3 customers. Decision: escalate to security; Tom to file security exception request with detailed audit plan by 10/08.

Action items (concrete, owner, due):
- Rajiv: deploy temporary higher-memory canary nodes + run expanded p99 memory profiling; due 2026-10-07.
- Marco/SRE (Liam): export 14-day load curve snapshot for autoscaler validation; due 2026-10-09.
- Tom: file Security Exception (installer KMS) with proposed narrow IP range and TTL; link in ticket; due 2026-10-08.
- Priya/QE: assign 2 testers for rollout UI and schedule smoke tests 10/08–10/09; due 2026-10-08.
- Sana/Product (Priya): compile extended pilot proposal + list of customer candidates for 8-bit quantization pilot extension; due 2026-10-12.
- Mei/Observability: patch request instrumentation to guarantee customer-route tag for embeddings/generation APIs (INF-3347); due 2026-10-11.

Risks & notes (brief):
- Risk: canary memory spike could cause mis-sample and hide regression modes. Mitigation: enlarge canary sample and include synthetic stress tests.
- Risk: if Security denies proxy exception, we must provide a fully manual installer path for the immediate customers — higher ops cost. Plan B: scheduled hands-on installs (Tom to prepare runbook).
- Note: We should avoid rolling back autoscaler changes globally; only canary/experimental pool should see new policy until validated.

Quick run of standup snippets (raw, unedited) — captures the real cadence / rough notes: 
- "Rajiv: seeing 12% mem bump at p99 on 512 seq when LC hits 3x baseline — hypothesis: slightly higher KV cache churn interacting with sharding path. TODO: reproduce with local shard-sim tool."
- "Sana: quantization logs — two customers dropped perf on sequence-heavy prompts; saving full tokens for 24h to investigate further. Might need per-customer profile toggles."
- "Tom: installer fails against proxy in gov-ne; manual injection works; need security exception... also, customers asking for HSM support — timeline? Research only."
- "Mei: cost dashboard looks good, but route tags null sometimes; we traced to older SDK versions used by some customers — will patch server-side guard to populate fallback tag."

Parking lot / longer-term topics (will be scheduled separately):
- Model multiplexing policies for multi-tenant GPU nodes (Mar 2026 spike doc referenced).
- Standardizing canary node instance types across cloud providers.
- Playbook for emergency fallback to smaller models when capacity constrained (Graceful degradation patterns).

Follow-ups / Who to update where:
- Rajiv: update this doc + post incident analysis draft to Confluence (link when ready).
- Marco: attach autoscaler CSV and sizing note to JIRA ENG-2412.
- Tom: post security exception request + backup manual install runbook to shared drive path /private-deployments/installer-runbooks.
- Priya: create QE story in JIRA for rollout UI verification and tag lead-eng.

Unresolved questions (for exec / cross-org attention):
- Do we want a formal gating policy that prevents full rollback of autoscaler changes without 48h of post-merge telemetry? (pros/cons discussed quickly; merits a separate session).
- How aggressive should we be in adding automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants when latency SLOs are threatened? (ops vs. quality tradeoff)

Meeting cadence notes: keep the weekly 60-minute slot with the current format for now; special deep dives to be scheduled bi-weekly for long-running cross-team efforts.

Appendix / quick references:
- Related tickets: ENG-2412 (autoscaler sizing), INF-3347 (observability tag bug), DEP-901 (private installer KMS).
- PRs: serving-runtime PR#1289 (shard+cache changes), autoscaler PR#467 (backoff policy), console PR#783 (A/B UI).
- Confluence: Batching Playbook (guidance for autoscaling + batching knobs), Canary Rollout Runbook.

Raw notes / scribbles captured during meeting (intentionally unpolished):
- "scale-up too fast -> thrash -> p99 jump"
- "we should sample more on dedicated, but cost — maybe sample windowed spikes"
- "fallback model list: gpt-small, gpt-medium (quantized)"
- "Priya: make the toggle visible to SRE? maybe no — keep behind flag for now"

Next meeting: 2026-10-13 09:30 PT. Please add items to the agenda in Slack thread #eng-leads by Tue 10/11.

If you have edits or missed captures, please update directly in this doc (collaborative): small edits ok; for substantive changes, send a PR to Aisha.

— end of digest —
